items.caseName: Commissioner HR & CE v. Rama Ravikumar
items.coram: Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi
items.headline: Thiruparankundram: HC findings stayed, one-time lamp lighting on Nov 24
items.text: The Court stayed the challenged findings of the Madras High Court's 6 January 2026 judgment on lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon near the dargah. As a one-off, it let a restricted Devasthanam team light the lamp on 24 November, with no public access, processions or construction, under the Madurai Collector's supervision. It said the arrangement creates no custom and left Article 25-26 questions open.

items.caseName: Tarun Gupta v. Rajendra Kumar Agarwal
items.coram: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: Notice on challenge to Allahabad HC verdict striking down UP Tenancy Act provisions
items.text: The Court issued notice on landlords' appeal against the Allahabad High Court ruling that struck down Sections 8, 9, 10, 38 and 42 of the UP Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021. Meanwhile, it directed that pending proceedings under the 2021 Act must not be dismissed as not maintainable or abated because of the High Court's verdict.

items.coram: Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N. Kotiswar Singh
items.headline: Karnataka's plea to restore bike taxi ban dismissed
items.text: The Court dismissed the Karnataka government's SLP against the High Court Division Bench ruling that set aside the State's ban on bike taxis. The bench remarked that regulating bike taxis is better than banning them, leaving intact the direction to consider permit applications subject to RTA conditions.

items.caseName: State of Tamil Nadu v. State of Karnataka
items.coram: Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh
items.headline: Tamil Nadu's pleas for release of 11 TMC Cauvery backlog rejected
items.text: The Court dismissed Tamil Nadu's applications seeking a direction to Karnataka to clear an 11 TMC Cauvery water backlog and release 1.3 TMC per day for ten days at Biligundlu. A further application to bring additional documents on record was also to be dismissed.

items.caseName: Shonee Kapoor v. Union of India
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana
items.headline: PIL for database of repeat sexual-offence complainants dismissed
items.text: The Court dismissed a PIL seeking district-level police databases of persons who repeatedly file sexual-offence complaints. It said everyone has a right to complain, false complaints already carry consequences, and such profiling could expose victims; existing safeguards like medical examination and magistrate statements suffice.

items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana
items.headline: Limited notice to Centre on awareness of consanguineous marriage risks
items.text: On a law student's plea flagging health risks of close-relative marriages, the Court issued notice to the Union for a limited purpose. It declined to direct legislation, asking only that the Centre consider a suitable law or wide publicity, including in school and college curricula.

items.caseName: Anand Arya v. Union of India
items.coram: Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi
items.headline: States told to set up wetland grievance committees forthwith
items.text: Noting submissions that court-protected wetlands are still being encroached, the Court directed all States to constitute Grievance Committees under Rule 5(6)(b) of the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 immediately. The order is to be circulated to all Chief Secretaries; the matter is next listed on 2 December 2026.

items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana
items.headline: Secretary General to probe why ED appeal went unlisted for three years
items.text: The Court ordered a fact-finding inquiry by its Secretary General into why ED's 2023 appeal against anticipatory bail granted in a PMLA case was not listed for nearly three years despite a re-listing order. It declined to entertain the appeal at this belated stage, as trial had begun, but said the High Court order would not serve as a precedent.

items.caseName: In Re: 135 Year Old Library, 8.5 Lakh Books - And No Room in the New Central Vista Plan
items.coram: Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva
items.headline: Central Secretariat Library case sent to CJI; no-shift undertaking continues
items.text: In the suo motu case on relocating the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library, the bench directed the matter be placed before the CJI for listing before an appropriate bench, as it was outside its roster. The Centre's undertaking not to move the library will continue until the next date.

items.headline: Murder charges against promoter in Garden Reach collapse (15 dead) not quashed
items.text: Justice Chaitali Chatterjee Das dismissed promoter Md. Wasim alias Wassi's revision against charges framed by the Alipore sessions court over the March 2024 Garden Reach building collapse. The charges include murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy.

items.caseName: Court on Its Own Motion v. State
items.headline: Bail for overstay does not legalise a foreign national's continued stay
items.text: A Division Bench held that bail granted to a foreign national accused of overstaying does not, by itself, legalise their continued stay in India. The matter concerned visas and detention centres.

items.headline: Voter ID / EPIC does not prove citizenship
items.text: The High Court held that a voter ID (Elector's Photo Identity Card) is not proof of citizenship. The case involved a woman declared a foreigner whose name appeared differently in electoral rolls.

items.headline: Marriage officer can't reject Special Marriage Act notice over party's customary divorce
items.text: The High Court held that a marriage officer cannot reject an inter-faith couple's notice of intended marriage under the Special Marriage Act just because one party earlier obtained a divorce through a customary deed.

items.caseName: Anushka Basavaraj Maidur v. National Testing Agency
items.headline: Scrapped exam cannot be revived to override merit in the exam that stood
items.text: The High Court held that a cancelled examination cannot be brought back to eclipse merit earned in the examination that survived.

items.caseName: Bar Council of Kerala v. Simy S.
items.headline: Reinstatement of former Bar Council secretary upheld; fraud finding changed to negligence
items.text: A Division Bench dismissed two writ appeals by the Bar Council of Kerala and its present Secretary against a single judge's ruling for former Secretary Simy S., whose service ended by a purported acceptance of resignation. It modified the single judge's finding of fraud against the Bar Council to one of negligence.

items.headline: Mayilpeely scholar exam allowed in schools, but results barred
items.text: The High Court allowed the Mayilpeely Young Scholar Examination 2026-27 to go ahead despite the State withdrawing permission. It barred the declaration of results.

items.headline: Library book procurement scam: contempt notice to two IAS officers
items.text: A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi issued contempt notice to IAS officers Chandramohan and Jayanthi over alleged disobedience of a 2024 judgment on public library book purchases. It advised state law officers not to defend the former Director and ordered the procurement files to be produced.
items.coram: Justice GR Swaminathan and Justice MD Sumathi

items.headline: Hindu–Christian marriage cannot be validated by registration under Hindu Marriage Act
items.text: A Division Bench held that a marriage between a Hindu and a non-Hindu cannot be solemnised under the Hindu Marriage Act or validated by registration, and declared such a marriage void. In the same matter, the bench said a person's religion cannot be inferred from their name or from Aadhaar, ration card or voter ID.
items.coram: Justice CV Karthikeyan and Justice S Raveekumar

items.headline: Bangladesh's challenge to GI tag for Bengal's Tangail saree to be heard
items.text: Justice PB Balaji dismissed a West Bengal weavers' society's application and declined to reject the Tangail Deputy Commissioner's petition against the GI tag for the Tangail saree. The main petition is listed on 7 December.

items.caseName: G. Kodeeswaran v. State of Tamil Nadu
items.headline: Parallel petition in Christian reservation case flagged as forum shopping
items.text: The Madurai Bench flagged an identical writ petition filed at the Principal Seat after it had already admitted the challenge on reservation for Christians as a backward class. It called this forum shopping.

items.headline: Asaram gets interim protection from arrest in FIR over late surrender after parole
items.text: Justice Sunil Beniwal granted Asaram interim protection from arrest in an FIR over his delay in returning to prison after parole expired. The court gave the public prosecutor time to obtain instructions on his quashing petition.

items.headline: Police have no authority to break citizens' bones in the name of official duty
items.text: The High Court restored cognizance against police officers accused of assaulting a petitioner and his mother during a visit linked to a warrant against his brother. It held that official duty is no cover for causing such injuries.

items.headline: Gratuity can't be denied to long-serving 'ad hoc' employee
items.text: A Division Bench of Chief Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao and Justice S. Datta Purkayastha held that an employee with nearly 33 years of continuous service cannot be treated as ad hoc to deny retiral benefits. It directed Tripura Horticulture Corporation Ltd to pay Rs 20 lakh gratuity with 7% interest.
items.coram: Chief Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao and Justice S. Datta Purkayastha

items.headline: 2019 POCSO amendment raising minimum sentence is not retrospective
items.text: The High Court cut a POCSO convict's sentence from 20 years to 10. The trial court had wrongly applied the higher minimum from the 2019 amendment to an offence committed before the amendment.
